Headlines in the condensed display face (Anton), small type in the grotesque (Archivo). The IPX one-sheet, 0.6 x 0.9 m: a thin rule, the IPX lozenge (at most 30 percent of the sheet height), the address "IPX.EXCHANGE", a thin rule. Nothing else: no slogan. Four colourways (paper / ink): 0 black / gold, 1 gold / black, 2 cream / black, 3 oxblood / cream. Placed: variant 1 three times (west hoarding, hoist tower, shop office), variant 3 twice (the cut, lot south wall), variant 2 once (vacant-lot hoarding); variant 0 exists but is not placed. Exact spots: spec 2.10.

name: SM_Sign_GraffitiSet
description: Spray paint and marker on walls, road and trucks: decals, no carrier. Paint misses the pits and joints of the wall (the web game masks 55 percent of it away); roughness 0.7. Three hands. Marker tag: fat-cap marker, slanted, letters a little off true, underlined in one stroke that ends in an arrowhead, three ticks over the last letter, a drip on three letters in ten; natural size about 0.42 m per letter wide x 0.9 m tall. Spray tag: soft edges, a faint wide overspray of the same letters, a ring thrown round the tag, flecks, long drips on nearly half the letters; same natural size. Throw-up: bubble letters, a fill inside a heavy near-black outline, a hard offset shadow, a white shine stroke on every letter, two four-point sparkles and a cloud of a second colour behind; about (0.62 m per letter + 0.5 m) wide x 1.4 m tall. Texts and colours on the block: "VULTURES" and "VLTR" in the crew's oxblood #8a1a22 (nine times, as marker, spray and throw-up); "HOLLIS" off-white marker (three); "QNS" cyan spray (two); "188" green throw-up (two) and pink spray (one); "QUEENS" cyan throw-up and gold marker; "NO SLEEP" violet throw-up 5.46 x 1.4 m; "JAMAICA AVE" green spray 4.62 x 0.9 m; "INC" gold marker; "RULE" gold spray 6.4 x 2.3 m across the mural. Two lie on the ground: "VULTURES" 3.4 x 1.0 m on the road at the first reel and 4.2 x 1.2 m on the court. Every box truck carries "RULE" (cream #e9e4d6) on one flank and "HOLLIS" (gold) on the other, fitted into 2.6 x 1.2 m. Sizes, positions and hands of all 23 wall and ground tags: spec 2.11. No real crew names, no real tags. The mural brief mural_ipx_rule in assets/level.json mentions four of them (RULE, HOLLIS, QUEENS, NO SLEEP): they are decals from this set, not part of the mural painting.

name: SM_Street_GroundDecals
description: Stains and damage on the ground, as decals with roughness. Oil: sump-oil patches 1.6 x 1.2 m, black at the heart with faint rainbow arcs at the rim, glossy (roughness 0.16), three shapes, 27 placed (parking lanes, shop floor, rear lane, lot). Cracks: a branching crack 2 x 0.6 m with crumbled shoulders, three shapes, 20 placed (roadway, lot). Grime: ground-in dirt 2 x 2 m, three shapes, 24 placed (gutters, alley, lane, shop floor). Scorch: a burnt-black blast mark with soot rays, 3 x 3 m, stretched to 5.5 x 4.2 m under the burned-out car in the vacant lot. Positions are seeded and exported (level.json, signage.placements).

name: SM_El_TrainCar
description: One car of the elevated train; five identical cars make the consist, coupled 0.7 m apart (79.8 m nose to tail), running at 16.5 m/s on the rails 6.83 m above the street. Forward = +X; pivot at the centre of the footprint on the rail top. Body 15.4 m long x 2.9 m wide x 3.55 m tall above the rail: floor 0.42 m above the rail, flat sides up to 3.29 m, then roof shoulders set in 0.42 m to a flat roof; an underframe box under the middle of the car (from 3.9 m inside each end, 0.14 to 0.42 m above the rail, 1.9 m wide); two trucks (bogies) 2.5 m long x 2.2 m wide centred 2.5 m from each end, with wheels, which the web game leaves as boxes. Each side: four pairs of sliding doors centred at 11.5, 37, 63 and 88.5 percent of the length, 1.31 m wide; a band of windows between them from 1.80 to 2.72 m above the rail. Each end: a door between two windows with an amber destination bar over it; two headlights and two red tail lights 0.85 m either side of the centre line, 1.2 m above the rail (the leading end of the consist shows white, the trailing end red). Finish: unpainted brushed stainless steel with fluted lower panels, a dark skirt, a blue belt line, a darker roof edge, street grime heavier toward the bottom. No operator name, no logo, no real route letter or number. Interior visible through the windows: fluorescent light, grab poles, seats, the odd rider as a silhouette; windows glow at night and are dim by day. It casts the moving shadow that darkens the avenue by day. Seen from below and from the sidewalk shed (hero view H7): the underside, trucks and third-rail shoes matter more than the roof.
colours: #f7ffee interior light through the windows (web radiance 1.9, 2.05, 1.75)
gameplay: none (no collision, cannot be shot; its pass shakes the camera and gusts loose paper)

name: SM_Architecture_FarWalkup
description: The next blocks beyond the play area: low-detail walk-up buildings seen only from inside the block, through haze, from just outside its walls to about 130 m beyond them. No collision, never entered. A kit, not one mesh: width 3 to 6 bays of 3.2 m (9.6 to 19.2 m), depth 14 to 19 m, a ground storey 4.1 m tall and upper storeys of 3.1 m, a parapet 0.6 to 1.4 m, flat tar roof. The size given is a typical one: 4 bays, 16 m deep, ground storey plus four floors. Heights by row: 10 to 20 m along the avenue's continuation (130 m past each end), 11 to 20 m for the backs across a 4 m alley behind the north and south edges, 17 to 30 m for a taller row 40 to 58 m further back, 10 to 22 m for the fronts on the two cross streets. Fronts on the avenue or a cross street: a ground row of roll-down gates (six in ten) and open shop fronts under coloured sign bands with no readable names, then rows of windows with stone lintels and sills, the odd blind, curtain and window air conditioner. Backs: plain windows. Side walls: blank brick. Four brick tints. Roof clutter: a water tower on a fifth to two fifths of the roofs (brief architecture_water_tower in props.json; here 3.1 m across, tank 3.1 m tall on 2.4 m legs, cone 1.1 m, scaled 0.85 to 1.15), a stair bulkhead 3 x 4 x 2.3 to 3 m on six roofs in ten, a chimney 0.7 x 0.7 x 1.5 to 3 m on four in ten. At night about a fifth of the windows are lit (tungsten, kitchen fluorescent, television blue, a red curtain) and 22 of them switch on and off. Pivot at the bottom-left corner of the street face, running along +X, face toward -Y. Plan rules: spec 2.18.
colours: #8c6050 sunlit brick of the day sheet

name: SM_Architecture_SkylineNear
description: The near skyline: a ring of city silhouette 215 m from the centre of the block and 72 m tall, three repeats of one strip round the circle, standing 3 m below street level so its foot is never seen. Roof line of flat-topped blocks of uneven height (the lowest a fifth of the strip height, most between a fifth and a half), the odd taller tower, roof tanks and masts. By day: sunlit stone and brick with darker glass, more than a third dissolved into the haze (36 percent, more at street level). By night: near-black bodies with one window dot in five lit (seven in ten warm, the rest cool; office floors stay lit in whole rows), half sunk into the haze, up to five red aviation lights on its tallest tops. Build as a ring of cards or as low-detail distant meshes; nothing on it may read as a real landmark.
materials: painted card or low-detail distant mesh, unlit

name: SM_Architecture_SkylineFar
description: The far skyline: a ring 395 m from the centre and 118 m tall that wraps once, lower and more even than the near ring except for a cluster of towers in the west (the far downtown, under the night glow and in front of the afternoon sun's quarter of the sky). By day blue-grey and more than half dissolved (56 percent); by night 26 percent of its window dots lit and three quarters sunk into the haze, with up to five red aviation lights. Dropped on the two lowest quality tiers of the web game. No real landmark silhouettes.
materials: painted card or low-detail distant mesh, unlit

name: SM_Fx_DebrisMasonry
description: Chips knocked out of asphalt, concrete, brick and dirt by bullets: a set of six small faceted lumps, 1.2 to 5 cm across (asphalt, concrete, brick 1.4 to 3.5 cm; dirt clods 2 to 5 cm), irregular, with one freshly broken face. Thrown as physics debris: 2 to 6 m/s off the surface, bounce up to three times, lie for 1.6 to 2.8 s and shrink away. One mesh set, tinted by surface. Up to 256 debris bodies of all kinds exist at once.

name: SM_Fx_DebrisWoodSplinters
description: Splinters torn out of timber by a bullet: four long slivers 0.8 to 1.6 cm thick and 3.5 to 6 times as long (about 3 to 10 cm), pale and fibrous, one end feathered. Five fly per hit at 2.5 to 7 m/s.

name: SM_Fx_DebrisGlassShards
description: Glass thrown by a shot through a pane: five small shards and cubes 1.2 to 3 cm across, pale blue-green, sharp-edged, catching the light. The web game shows twelve glinting crosses 3.5 to 9 cm that tumble (spin up to 14 rad/s), fall and wink out within a second, plus two solid chips; the mesh set replaces the chips and can carry the glints as a sparkle on its facets.
materials: window glass, clear with a green edge

name: SM_Fx_DebrisMetalScrap
description: Small scraps of sheet metal and plastic: paint chips off a car body 1.2 to 2.5 cm, bits of a Buzzard's shell 1.5 to 3.5 cm on a hit, and four lumps 3 to 9 cm (up to twice as long) when a Buzzard is killed. Five bent, torn pieces, one mesh set tinted by source.

name: SM_Fx_DebrisBlastFragments
description: Fragments thrown by an exploding propane tank or welding rack: six charred, torn pieces of steel plate and fittings, 4 to 11 cm across and up to 2.4 times as long, near-black to dark grey. Thirteen fly per tank blast at 3 to 11 m/s outward and 3 to 10 m/s upward, bounce, and lie for 2.2 to 4 s. (The tank halves themselves are the wreck briefs in props.json.)
gameplay: none (cosmetic; blast damage is computed separately)

name: SM_Fx_PaperSheet
description: A loose sheet of newspaper, 0.22 x 0.30 m, lying on the avenue: seven of them slide, lift up to 0.28 m and tumble when a gust or a train passes. Two-sided; a soft, slightly creased page: a dark headline bar across the top (8 to 20 percent down, 80 percent of the width), ragged lines of grey text below it, a faint brown stain band across the page. No readable words in the web game; if a masthead is wanted it is the block's own invented paper, "QUEENS NIGHT LEDGER". A flat sheet with a few bend loops so it can curl as it tumbles.
gameplay: none (slides round cars and walls, no collision with players)

name: SK_Pigeon
description: A city pigeon in flight, seen from below against the sky at 15 to 34 m: 20 birds in three flocks wheel over the roofs by day. Web size: body 0.46 m long, wingspan 0.75 m (a real rock pigeon is about 0.34 m long with a 0.68 m span; the height given is a modelling choice). Forward = +X. Needs a flap cycle (wings beat at about 15 to 19 rad/s in bursts) and a glide pose with the wings held out; banks into its turn. The web game draws near-black silhouettes; a lit grey bird with darker wing bars and a paler rump reads the same at that distance. Perched and startled birds (art bible) are an addition with no web behaviour.
materials: feathers (simple shaded mesh; alpha cards for wing tips if needed)

name: SM_Fx_DecalBulletHoles
description: Bullet-hole decal set, one design per surface group, each with base colour, normal and opacity (the art bible asks for parallax or mesh-backed holes, not flat stickers). Sizes are the diameter of the whole mark. Stone (asphalt 0.24 to 0.34 m, concrete 0.25 to 0.36 m): a dark pit about a fifth of the diameter, a ragged crater of freshly broken pale material, a sooty powder halo. Brick (0.25 to 0.36 m): the same with broken faces in brick red. Metal (0.12 to 0.17 m; car bodies to 0.18 m): a black hole about a sixth of the diameter, a rim of bare bright metal, flaked paint, a little soot. Glass (0.30 to 0.46 m): a small hole, a crushed white ring, nine radial cracks joined by two rings. Wood (0.15 to 0.22 m): a dark hole with pale splinters torn out along the grain, which runs vertically. Soot (rubber 0.08 to 0.12 m, dirt 0.20 to 0.30 m, cloth 0.07 to 0.10 m): a dark smudge with a small hole. Random roll except wood. 256 marks at most, the oldest replaced; none on characters.
gameplay: none (marks only; no penetration is modelled)

name: SM_Fx_DecalScorch
description: Blast scorch on the ground, two designs: a burnt-black heart about 40 percent of the diameter, soot streaks thrown outward to between half and nine tenths of the radius, a brown singed fringe. Drawn 3.4 to 4.3 m across for a propane tank, scaled with the blast (about 1.6 to 2 m for a Buzzard, up to 5 m for a welding rack), opacity 0.92, random roll. Matt soot over whatever is there; one is left under every blast whose centre is less than 2.2 x scale + 0.6 m above the ground (2.8 m for a tank).

name: SM_Fx_FlipbookFireball
description: Flipbook source for a Niagara sprite effect: simulate in Blender (smoke and fire domain) and render to a sprite sheet with its lighting channels (for example six-way light maps), not baked colour. The web game uses hand-painted static sprites, so there is no flipbook to match, only the motion and sizes below. The fireball of a propane blast at scale 1: one white-hot frame 2.2 m across, then tongues of flame thrown outward at 3.5 to 12 m/s that slow within a metre or two, swell from about 1 m to 2.3 to 3.4 m, redden from orange to deep red and burn out in 0.3 to 0.7 s, with a slower core (1.6 to 2.1 m swelling to 3.4 to 4.4 m, 0.55 to 0.85 s) that holds the centre and lifts. A ball of fire 4 to 5 m across that rises and blackens in under a second. Two variants so repeats do not match. Scales with the blast: 0.46 for a Buzzard (half the flame, with blue-white electric sparks), 1.15 for a welding rack.
materials: fire and soot simulation, rendered sprite sheet
colours: #edad61 flame at birth (web linear 0.85, 0.42, 0.12; many sprites sum to white)
gameplay: explosive: visual of the blast only (damage radius 6.5 m for a tank, 7.5 m for a rack)

name: SM_Fx_FlipbookSmokeColumn
description: Flipbook source for a Niagara sprite effect: simulate in Blender (smoke and fire domain) and render to a sprite sheet with its lighting channels (for example six-way light maps), not baked colour. The web game uses hand-painted static sprites, so there is no flipbook to match, only the motion and sizes below. Rolling black smoke of a fuel blast. Puffs are born 0.9 m across inside the fireball, glowing orange from within for the first half second, roll outward at up to 3.4 m/s and up at 1.2 to 5.6 m/s, swell to 2.8 to 4 m and thin out over 2.6 to 4.8 s; a column of bigger puffs (to 5.6 m) climbs at 3 to 7.5 m/s for 4.5 to 6.5 s and leans with the wind. Sooty black-brown by day (it must stand out against a bright sky), dark grey at night, lit by the sun or the lamps. Three puff variants. The same puffs, smaller and fewer, serve burning Buzzards and smouldering wreckage.
materials: smoke simulation, rendered sprite sheet with light maps
colours: #605d5b young smoke albedo at night (web linear 0.07 to 0.15; 45 percent darker by day)

name: SM_Fx_FlipbookDust
description: Flipbook source for a Niagara sprite effect: simulate in Blender (smoke and fire domain) and render to a sprite sheet with its lighting channels (for example six-way light maps), not baked colour. The web game uses hand-painted static sprites, so there is no flipbook to match, only the motion and sizes below. Dust knocked off a surface: a fast jet along the surface normal (3.5 to 6 m/s, 0.1 m swelling to 0.6 m, gone in 0.3 to 0.45 s) and a slower cloud that hangs (0.16 m swelling to 0.95 m over 0.65 to 1.05 s). Also the low rolling ring a blast kicks along the ground (0.7 m swelling to 1.9 to 2.7 m, racing out at 7 to 11.5 m/s) and the puff at the feet on a hard landing. Three variants: a soft grainy cloud, a ground-hugging roll, a scatter of lint and fibres for hits on cloth and bodies. Tinted per surface; lit by the scene.
materials: dust simulation, rendered sprite sheet with light maps
colours: #9a6a64 body-hit puff (cloth dust with a faint dark-red tint, nothing wet)

name: SM_Fx_FlipbookSteam
description: Flipbook source for a Niagara sprite effect: simulate in Blender (smoke and fire domain) and render to a sprite sheet with its lighting channels (for example six-way light maps), not baked colour. The web game uses hand-painted static sprites, so there is no flipbook to match, only the motion and sizes below. Steam from a manhole or vent stack: a thin white column that rises 6.2 m in about 5 s (fast out of the grate, then slowing), drifts 1.5 m sideways and leans with the wind, each puff growing from 0.3 to 0.55 m to between 1.3 and 2.6 m. See-through: you look through it at the street. White in sun, grey when front-lit, the colour of the nearest lamp at night. Six columns on the block. Two variants.
materials: vapour simulation, rendered sprite sheet with light maps
colours: #eaebef sunlit steam of the day rig (web linear 0.82, 0.83, 0.86)
gameplay: none (does not block sight lines for the enemies; thin enough to see through)

name: SM_Fx_FlipbookPropaneJet
description: Flipbook source for a Niagara sprite effect: simulate in Blender (smoke and fire domain) and render to a sprite sheet with its lighting channels (for example six-way light maps), not baked colour. The web game uses hand-painted static sprites, so there is no flipbook to match, only the motion and sizes below. The roaring jet of a hit propane tank or welding rack during its fuse (1.6 s for a tank, 1.1 s for a rack): a tight blue-white cone at the valve or the bullet hole, 7 to 20 cm wide, turning into an orange tongue that slows, swells to 0.36 to 0.52 m, curls upward and breaks up, with sparks spat along it. It lengthens as the pressure builds: about 1.0 m growing to 1.7 m on a tank, 1.35 m growing to 2.25 m on a rack. Forward = +X from the valve. It throws a flickering orange light (range 7.5 m).
gameplay: explosive: the visible warning that the tank is about to blow
